trials.role: Intravenous NAMI-A monotherapy in advanced solid tumours
trials.outcome: 24 treated. MTD and recommended dose: 300 mg/m²/day by 3-hour infusion for 5 days every 21 days. Painful, prolonged blisters on hands and feet first appeared at 400 mg/m²/day. An infusion hypersensitivity reaction at 300 mg/m²/day met DLT criteria in one patient.
31 evaluated for toxicity. MTD with gemcitabine was 300 mg/m² of NAMI-A on the 28-day schedule and 450 mg/m² on the 21-day schedule. Neutropenia with dose holds was dose limiting on both schedules.

logp.method_description: The lipophilicity of ruthenium(II) complexes 1–3 and NAMI-A was determined using the shake-flask method.56 Before experiments aqueous (0.9% v/v) sodium chloride and organic (1-octanol) phases were saturated for 1 week. All the ruthenium complexes were dissolved at a concentration of 0.30 mg mL-l in 2.5 mL of the aqueous phase and an equal volume of the organic phase was added. Next, the solution was mechanically mixed in plastic tubes for 30 min, followed by centrifugation (6000 rpm, 15 min). After separation, the aqueous phases were analysed using UV–Vis spectroscopy to determine the amount of the compound in the measured phase. The absorption values before and after shaking were compared. The partition coefficient (logPo/w) for each compound was calculated based on the Lambert–Beer law to determine the logPo/w values. For each complex, the procedure was repeated three times. Selected wavelengths for 1–3 and NAMI-A at which the absorbance maximum was observed, epsilon at the wavelength chosen and standard deviation for determining logPo/w values are presented in Table S1.

The octanol–water partition coefficients were determined by a modified shake-flask method (Cirri et al. 2017, Marzo et al. 2017). Water (250 mL, distilled after Milli-Q purification) and n-octanol (250 mL) were shaken together for 72 h to allow saturation of both phases in a 500 mL flask. The suspension was allowed to separate at least for one week in the dark. A solution of the complexes was prepared using the water phase (3 × 10-3 M) and an equal volume of octanol was added. Biphasic solutions were mixed for ten minutes and then centrifuged at 25 °C with an MPW-260R centrifuge equipped with a 11,746 rotor for 5 min at 6000 rpm to allow separation. Concentrations in both phases were determined through UV–Vis or ICP-AES spectroscopy depending on the properties of each complex. Reported logP values are defined as log10([complex]oct/[complex]wat). Final values were reported as mean of three determinations.
